introduction: Michigan EITC is a refundable income-tax credit for eligible workers. Claim it on MI-1040 after claiming federal EITC.
description: Michigan EITC is a refundable income-tax credit for eligible workers. Claim it on MI-1040 after claiming federal EITC.

sections.who: Federal EITC eligibility is required, with Michigan residency or qualifying Michigan-income rules. Both returns must be filed even if otherwise unnecessary.
sections.get: The state credit is 30% of the eligible federal EITC. Income, filing status and qualifying children affect the underlying calculation.
sections.docs:
• Federal return and EITC calculation.
  • Wage and self-employment records.
  • Residency or Michigan-source income information.
sections.apply:
1. Confirm federal eligibility

    Use the resources linked from Michigan Treasury’s EITC page.

  2. File the federal return

    Claim the eligible federal credit.

  3. File MI-1040

    Claim Michigan EITC using the instructions for that tax year and keep the calculation.
sections.after: For an older return, use year-specific amendment and filing guidance rather than assuming current procedures apply.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using Michigan EITC eligibility and filing. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Yes. Michigan says federal EITC eligibility is required.
